sha_note: SAME SHA as R63 (and R62). Three consecutive runs at a6805b1: R62 all-pass/0.0 swap, R63 all-pass/6.0 swap, R64 BREACH/31.3 swap.
gate_failures: Phase 3b RULER (memory breach at vt@16K chain=4)
Phase 5 Memory Profile (swap peak 31.3 GB > 12.9 GB limit)
dedup_override_reason: Same SHA but dramatically different result. R62 had 0.0 GB swap. R63 had 6.0 GB. R64 hit 31.3 GB — highest ever observed. Dedup override applies: this is a catastrophic co-tenancy event, not noise.

breach_details.swap_peak_note: HIGHEST EVER. Previous record was R58's 12.9 GB (exactly at limit). R64 is 2.4x the limit. Something external consumed ~20 GB of memory mid-run.
breach_details.task_85_note: 5th analyst-filed task SHIPPED and observed working in production. The sentinel line appeared right after the ERROR log, clean and grep-able.

profiler_under_breach.cpu_scheduling_note: 92.91% — down from clean-box 0.9932 (R61). 7% of wall-clock was swap-thrashing, not computing. Task #80's metric correctly flags the problem.
profiler_under_breach.cpu_avg_note: Only 20% CPU utilization — the process spent most of its time waiting on memory I/O, not computing. On a clean run CPU avg is ~50%.
profiler_under_breach.swap_io_peak_note: 13 GB/s instantaneous swap I/O — 30x the M4 Pro's physical ceiling. Profiler sampler artifact at its most extreme, confirming that heavier pressure produces larger artifacts.
profiler_under_breach.results_json_note: FIRST breach run in this session where Phase 6 Summary ran and wrote results.json + profile.json. The Phase 3b→Phase 5/6 cascade path works correctly post-breach — we get full profiler data even when the run fails.

warmup_note: 4.0s — clean range, meaning the system was OK at startup. The external memory load appeared mid-run, not at launch. This is exactly the failure mode that Task #86 (per-phase headroom re-check) was designed to catch.

quality_metrics_partial.ruler_partial: 7/11 PASS before breach (multi_key@4K 2/2+4/4, multi_key@16K 3/3+5/5, 64K SKIP, vt@4K chain=3 1/1 + chain=4 1/1, vt@16K chain=4 BREACH)

analyst_observations.same_sha_three_outcomes: R62/R63/R64 all at SHA a6805b1. R62: 0.0 GB swap, all pass. R63: 6.0 GB swap, all pass. R64: 31.3 GB swap, breach. The duo cache code is unchanged — all three outcomes are from different co-tenancy states on the same 48 GB laptop. This is the most dramatic demonstration yet of the co-tenancy sensitivity documented in R59.
analyst_observations.task_85_shipped_and_working: The WATCHDOG-BREACH sentinel line from Task #85 appeared in the console output for the first time. Engineers shipped it (commit unknown — need to check git log for the Task #85 implementation). 5th analyst-filed task shipped in this session (61, 62, 71, 80, 85). 100% pickup rate continues.
analyst_observations.first_breach_with_full_profiler_data: R54/R57/R58 all breached or crashed without writing results.json (Phase 6 never ran). R64 is the first breach where the cascade path correctly routed to Phase 5/6 Summary, giving us full profiler data under failure conditions. cpu_scheduling_fraction 0.9291 and cpu_avg_pct 19.5% are the forensic fingerprints of a swap-thrashed run.
analyst_observations.task_86_would_have_helped: The warmup was 4.0s (clean). Pre-flight passed (34 GB free). But by the time RULER vt@16K chain=4 ran (~7 min later), swap had grown to 17.9 GB. Task #86 (per-phase headroom re-check) would have caught this mid-run and skipped the RULER 16K tasks instead of breaching.
